description:
The UK government has approved plans for China to build its largest embassy in Europe in central London.
The decision has alarmed activists and MPs, who warn the site could be used to intimidate dissidents and enable surveillance.
Pro-democracy activists from Hong Kong say they fear harassment, abduction and increased monitoring in Britain.
Lawmakers also raise concerns about the embassy’s proximity to fibre-optic cables carrying sensitive financial and public data.
UK security services have warned of Chinese influence operations, though they have not formally opposed the plans.
China denies spying or harassment, while London insists security will not be compromised despite seeking closer trade ties.
Critics say the move risks making Britain feel less safe for those who sought refuge there.

Al Jazeera’s Milena Veselinovic reports from London.

The pause in fighting is intended to allow time for the SDF to explore integration of Hasakah province through diplomatic channels. 
Olabi said Syria has been working constructively for a year and has already proposed several plans, stressing they do not want to speculate on what happens if the ceasefire lapses. The ceasefire is framed as a step towards a longer-term deal, with both sides under pressure to avoid a return to conflict.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The UN’s nuclear watchdog says Ukraine’s Chernobyl plant has lost all off-site power after Russian strikes hit the electricity grid.
The IAEA warns that several substations vital for nuclear safety were damaged, affecting power supplies to multiple nuclear facilities.
Although Chernobyl’s reactor exploded in 1986, external electricity is still needed to safely manage nuclear waste at the site.
Ukraine’s foreign minister accuses Russia of deliberately targeting energy infrastructure linked to nuclear facilities.
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi says the agency is closely monitoring risks to plants including Rivne and South Ukraine.
He says experts remain deployed across Ukraine to help prevent accidents amid widespread power disruptions.
The IAEA stresses the situation is delicate, with nuclear safety dependent on restoring stable electricity supplies.

Al Jazeera’s Hashem Ahelbarra reports from Davos.

Fighting around two prisons holding thousands of ISIL detainees has exposed one of Syria's most dangerous unresolved legacies. 
Dozens have been killed as the Kurdish-led SDF withdrew from areas it controlled for years, with Syrian government forces moving in immediately. 
The SDF manages facilities holding around 60,000 people at their peak, now reduced but still including roughly 40,000 at Al Hol camp alone. 
Human Rights Watch says approximately 18,000 detainees are foreign nationals from more than 60 countries, whilst most Western nations refuse to repatriate adult male fighters. 
As prison guard units thin and the SDF appeals for reinforcements, experts warn the crisis remains one prison break away from catastrophe.

Al Jazeera's Osama bin Javaid reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Israel have demolished buildings inside the headquarters of the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) in occupied East Jerusalem, as the far-right government clamps down heavily on humanitarian groups that provide desperately needed aid to Palestinians in Gaza.
UNRWA said in a statement on Tuesday that Israeli forces had confiscated staff devices and forced them out of their headquarters in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood.
Israel's parliament passed a law in October 2024 banning the agency from operating in the country,
It also prohibited Israeli officials from having contact with the agency.
UNRWA chief Philippe Lazzarini, said the attack came “in the wake of other steps taken by Israeli authorities to erase the Palestine Refugee identity”.
He also warned that “what happens today to UNRWA will happen tomorrow to any other international organisation or diplomatic mission” anywhere in the world.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank
title: Israel demolishes UNRWA buildings in occupied East Jerusalem

description:
The Syrian army and Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) are accusing each other of violating the ceasefire
It follows outbreaks of fighting despite an agreement announced on Sunday.
Syria's army is accusing the SDF of releasing a number of ISIL prisoners, that had been held in the al-Shaddadi prison in Hasakah province. Government says 81 of the 120 escapees have been rearrested.
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa met with SDF chief Mazloum Abadi in Damascus on Monday, but there was no statement issued after the meeting.
Al-Sharaa has also held a phone call with US President Donald Trump on the need for unity in Syria.

Al Jazeera’s Ayman Oghanna has more on their meeting as well as President al-Sharaa's phone call with Donald Trump and Zein Basravi is following developments from Aleppo, in northern Syria.
